scoring_justification: Absolute energies and radial distribution shapes cannot be re-derived without re-running the full simulation; therefore structural checks (peak location conditions, melting signature) with thresholds from the paper's figures are used.

outputs.description: The caloric curve (average potential energy vs temperature) for Na+(H2O)20. The hidden checker will verify the presence of a steep energy increase (melting transition) within an expected temperature window.

Ion radial distribution function at low and high temperatures. The checker will verify that the distribution peaks at a larger radius at 150 K and a smaller radius at 350 K, consistent with a transition from surface to interior solvation.

hidden_assets.purpose: Thresholds for caloric curve melting detection (temperature range and energy increase)
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from the paper's Figure 4: the heat capacity peak and sigmoidal increase shown around 235 K with energy difference between solid and liquid states of ~45 kcal/mol.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Read from the paper's figure description and text; temperature window widened to 200-260 K to allow stochastic variation; minimum energy increase set to 30 kcal/mol to be conservative.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Directly based on the paper's reported observation of a melting transition with a sigmoidal energy increase near 235 K.

hidden_assets.purpose: Thresholds for ion radial distribution peak positions at 150 K (surface) and 350 K (interior)
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from paper's Figure 3 and associated text: at 150 K the Na+ peak appears at ~4.0 Å, while at 350 K it shifts to near the center (~1.8 Å).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Set thresholds >3.5 Å for low T and <2.5 Å for high T based on the reported peak positions and qualitative description.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Directly based on the paper's reported structural transition from surface to interior solvation.

steps.description: Check caloric curve for presence of melting transition: temperature of maximum energy slope in 200-260 K and total energy increase > 30 kcal/mol.
Check that Na+ radial distribution peak at 150 K is at radius > 3.5 Angstrom (surface) and at 350 K is at radius < 2.5 Angstrom (interior).
